glossary.title: Temperature
glossary.note: A setting that controls how creative or predictable an AI's answers are. Low = safe and consistent, high = more varied.

extra.definition: A setting that controls how creative or predictable an AI's answers are. Low = safe and consistent, high = more varied.

glossary.title: Inference
glossary.note: Using a trained AI model to get an answer. Every time you send a prompt, the model runs inference.

extra.definition: Using a trained AI model to get an answer. Every time you send a prompt, the model runs inference.

glossary.title: Parameters
glossary.note: The millions or billions of numbers inside a model that it learned during training. More parameters usually means a bigger, more capable model.

extra.definition: The millions or billions of numbers inside a model that it learned during training. More parameters usually means a bigger, more capable model.

glossary.title: Reasoning model
glossary.note: An AI model that "thinks" step by step before answering, which helps with maths, code and planning but takes longer.

extra.definition: An AI model that "thinks" step by step before answering, which helps with maths, code and planning but takes longer.

glossary.title: Transformer
glossary.note: The design behind almost all modern language models. It lets the model look at every word in a sentence at once to understand context.

extra.definition: The design behind almost all modern language models. It lets the model look at every word in a sentence at once to understand context.

glossary.title: System prompt
glossary.note: Hidden instructions given to an AI before your message, setting its role, tone and rules.

extra.definition: Hidden instructions given to an AI before your message, setting its role, tone and rules.

glossary.title: Few-shot prompting
glossary.note: Showing the AI a few examples of what you want inside your prompt so it copies the pattern.

extra.definition: Showing the AI a few examples of what you want inside your prompt so it copies the pattern.

glossary.title: Guardrails
glossary.note: Rules and checks around an AI app that block unsafe, off-topic or wrong outputs.

extra.definition: Rules and checks around an AI app that block unsafe, off-topic or wrong outputs.

glossary.title: Benchmark
glossary.note: A standard test used to compare AI models, like an exam everyone takes.

extra.definition: A standard test used to compare AI models, like an exam everyone takes.

glossary.title: Overfitting
glossary.note: When a model memorises its training examples instead of learning general patterns, so it does badly on new data.

extra.definition: When a model memorises its training examples instead of learning general patterns, so it does badly on new data.

glossary.title: Quantization
glossary.note: Shrinking a model by storing its numbers with less precision, so it runs faster on smaller computers with a small quality loss.

extra.definition: Shrinking a model by storing its numbers with less precision, so it runs faster on smaller computers with a small quality loss.

glossary.title: Distillation
glossary.note: Training a small, cheap model to copy the answers of a big model.

extra.definition: Training a small, cheap model to copy the answers of a big model.

glossary.title: Grounding
glossary.note: Making an AI base its answer on specific trusted sources (like your documents) instead of only its memory.

extra.definition: Making an AI base its answer on specific trusted sources (like your documents) instead of only its memory.

glossary.title: Knowledge cutoff
glossary.note: The date after which a model has no training data, so it doesn't know about later events unless given search or documents.

extra.definition: The date after which a model has no training data, so it doesn't know about later events unless given search or documents.

glossary.title: Human in the loop
glossary.note: A setup where a person reviews or approves the AI's work before it takes effect.

extra.definition: A setup where a person reviews or approves the AI's work before it takes effect.

glossary.title: Deepfake
glossary.note: A fake image, video or voice made with AI to look or sound like a real person.

extra.definition: A fake image, video or voice made with AI to look or sound like a real person.

glossary.title: Synthetic data
glossary.note: Artificial data created by computers or AI, used to train or test models when real data is scarce or private.

extra.definition: Artificial data created by computers or AI, used to train or test models when real data is scarce or private.

glossary.title: AGI
glossary.note: Artificial general intelligence: a hypothetical AI that can learn and do almost any intellectual task a person can.

extra.definition: Artificial general intelligence: a hypothetical AI that can learn and do almost any intellectual task a person can.

projects.title: AI course-notes and flashcard builder for students

project.title: AI course-notes and flashcard builder for students
project.problem: Students record lectures and download slides but never turn them into revision material before exams.
project.solution: Upload a lecture recording, slides or PDF and get clean notes, a one-page summary and spaced-repetition flashcards that export to Anki.
project.customer: University and exam-prep students; tutors who resell it to their classes.
project.revenue: Freemium: 3 uploads a month free, $6/month student plan; bulk licences for tutoring centres.
steps: Accept PDF, slides and audio uploads
Generate notes and question–answer cards with an LLM
Add a shared class deck and payments
project.watch: Respect lecture copyright: only process material the student is allowed to use, and never publish shared decks publicly by default.

projects.title: AI accessibility checker for small-business websites

project.title: AI accessibility checker for small-business websites
project.problem: Accessibility laws (ADA in the US, the European Accessibility Act from June 2025) put small businesses at legal risk, but audits are expensive.
project.solution: Scan a website with an open-source checker, then use AI to explain each issue in plain English, suggest fixed code and write missing alt text.
project.customer: Small businesses, web agencies and freelance web designers.
project.revenue: $29–99/month per site with monthly re-scans; white-label reports for agencies.
steps: Run axe-core on each page with Playwright
Ask an LLM for plain-English explanations and code fixes
Generate alt text for images with a vision model
project.watch: Automated scans catch only part of accessibility problems; say so clearly and never promise legal compliance.

projects.title: Grant and tender finder with AI-drafted applications

project.title: Grant and tender finder with AI-drafted applications
project.problem: Non-profits and small firms miss grants and public tenders because finding and writing applications takes days.
project.solution: Watch public grant and tender portals, match new calls to each client's profile, and draft a first-pass application from their past documents.
project.customer: Non-profits, research groups and small businesses bidding for public contracts.
project.revenue: $49–199/month subscription, or a success fee for done-for-you applications.
steps: Pull new calls from open portals (Grants.gov, TED for EU tenders)
Score each call against a client profile with embeddings
Send a weekly shortlist by email
Draft answers from the client's past applications (RAG)
Add a review-and-export step for Word/PDF
project.watch: A person must review every application before it is submitted; never let the AI invent facts or figures.
